articles.headline: Bears call on QB3 Case Keenum in rousing victory over Eagles
articles.description: In his first NFL start in 1,009 days, Chicago third-string quarterback Case Keenum, 38, led the Bears to a dominant 27-7 victory over the perennial NFC heavyweight Philadelphia Eagles on Monday, a performance coach Ben Johnson labeled "extraordinary."
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- The night belonged to Case Keenum. And so did a game ball.

After leading the Chicago Bears to a dominant 27-7 win over the perennial NFC heavyweight Philadelphia Eagles -- which marked his first start in 1,009 days -- Keenum was handed the commemorative football and the floor in the postgame locker room at Soldier Field.

With quarterbacks Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent looking on behind him, Keenum delivered a passionate postgame speech about his 67th career start. He talked about how his opportunities to play meaningful football had routinely been taken away and how he discovered his love for the game again after coach Ben Johnson brought him out of retirement to be a part of Chicago's quarterback room in 2025.

Amid Williams' Grade 2 hamstring strain that is expected to keep him out 3-4 weeks, and Bagent not clearing the NFL's concussion protocol until Sunday, the Bears turned to their third-string quarterback to get their second win of the season.

"It's all about Case Keenum and what he was able to do here tonight," coach Ben Johnson said. "I thought he did an extraordinary job."

At 38 years and 223 days old, Keenum became the second-oldest quarterback in franchise history to win a start (Todd Collins has him beat by 116 days). Chicago's 20-point win was its largest on Monday Night Football since Week 15 of the 2010 season at the Vikings.

Keenum didn't resemble a backup quarterback simply trying to keep his team afloat in the absence of its starter. He accounted for three touchdowns and zero turnovers in the win, leading Chicago on an 11-play, 66-yard opening drive that ended with Keenum finding Luther Burden III for an 8-yard touchdown.

Keenum later connected with Kalif Raymond on a 41-yard touchdown late in the third quarter and dove into the end zone on a 1-yard quarterback sneak. He has won games as a starting quarterback with seven different franchises, which is tied with his former Texans teammate Ryan Fitzpatrick for the most in NFL history.

"Playing well anytime in your career feels good," Keenum said. "To do it on Monday Night Football after you thought you weren't ever going to play again multiple times. Golly, this is special. It's really special. And I don't know if I'll be able to put it into words tonight, but I'm going to enjoy it tonight, that's for sure."

Keenum orchestrated an offensive performance that relied on its passing attack. As the Eagles sold out to stop Chicago's run game, Keenum completed 24 of 34 attempts for 247 yards and two touchdowns.

He showed poise in the face of pressure. The results of the 12 blitzes sent by Philadelphia defensive coordinator Vic Fangio were disastrous for the Eagles: Keenum finished 11-of-11 for 145 yards and two touchdowns when the Eagles sent added rushers.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィーク中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク期間中に発生したプレミアリーグ主力選手の負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデート。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Man City CEO adamant legal battle with the Premier League is not over
articles.description: Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told his fellow European club bosses the already lengthy legal battle with the Premier League will take "a lot more time" to conclude.
articles.body:
Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told his fellow European club bosses the already lengthy legal battle with the Premier League will take "a lot more time" to conclude.

News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of 115 charges they faced of breaching the league's financial rules, immediately sparking speculation they could face unprecedented sanctions.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak told supporters in an open letter published on Saturday that the club were "confident" of proving their innocence, and chief executive Soriano addressed the elephant in the room when he met fellow members of the European Football Clubs board in Copenhagen on Monday.

The Press Association understands Soriano said at the end of the EFC board meeting that he felt he had to say something given Friday's news, that City disagreed with the ruling but remained confident of winning and that the club were still fighting.

Sources in the meeting said Soriano then remarked: "It's taken eight years to get here, and it's going to take a lot more time."

The "eight years" Soriano referred to was the opening of the league's investigation into City in 2018.

Soriano, who declined to answer media questions as he exited the meeting, made the comments in the presence of some other English top-flight bosses, with Manchester United's chief of international football relations Jean-Claude Blanc and Everton owner Dan Friedkin -- there in his capacity as owner of Roma -- also attending the meeting in the Danish capital.

Among the alleged breaches, all strenuously denied by City, was a charge of failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini's pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

The 61-year-old, now in back in charge of Italy for a second stint, was quizzed about the charges at a press conference ahead of Monday's Nations League match with Turkey in Bursa.

He said: "It's not an issue that concerns me. It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years."

The Premier League has declined to comment since news of the verdict emerged last week, and Mancini continued: "Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

City were charged with failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons from 2009 -- the year Mancini took over.

They were also charged with failing to provide full details of remuneration in contracts with players between 2010-11 and 2015-16, and with failing to co-operate with the Premier League's investigation over a period from 2018 to 2023.

A City spokesperson said on Friday: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

articles.headline: Sirianni regrets reaction to hit on QB Hurts in Eagles' loss
articles.description: After a 27-7 loss to Chicago on Monday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni expressed "remorse" over his reaction to a sideline hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson on Philadelphia's Jalen Hurts that temporarily knocked his quarterback out of the first half.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni expressed "remorse" over his reaction to the sideline hit by Chicago Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson on Jalen Hurts that temporarily knocked his quarterback out of the game midway through the second quarter Monday night.

Cameras showed Sirianni appearing to shout expletives toward Jackson after the play.

"Obviously, you want to always fight for your players, and protect your players. I always come away when I have a moment like that with remorse of, 'Man, I shouldn't have let my emotions get the best of me,'" Sirianni said after the Eagles' 27-7 loss.

Facing a second-and-4 deep in Chicago territory, Hurts scrambled to the right sideline and began stepping out of bounds by the first-down marker. Jackson hit him hard in the shoulder area, sending Hurts crashing to the turf, and was whistled for unnecessary roughness.

Hurts got up and rejoined his teammates, but the referees stepped in and directed Hurts off the field to be tested for a concussion.

Andy Dalton took over at quarterback and threw an interception on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, denying the Eagles their first points of the game.

"I apologized to [Hurts]," Dalton said. "I put us in a bad spot, but I put him in a bad spot, too."

Hurts left the medical tent to watch the third-down play unfold, but he had not yet been cleared. Moments later, he received the go-ahead to return to action. Hurts was visibly upset as he exited the tent and made his way toward the bench.

"I was just waiting for the thumbs-up. I felt fine; we already checked it," he said. "I don't know the extent of the process; obviously, wish we could have expedited things. I know I felt fine."

Sirianni said, "I get nothing," when asked what type of information he was receiving about Hurts' status in that moment. "They need to go through their process there. You think about maybe calling a timeout in a situation like that ... but if you call a timeout, I have no idea what's going on and when he's going to come out.

"I think that's the right way to go about it because you don't want to influence anything. The health of the player is the most important thing."

Hurts returned the following series and orchestrated an eight-play, 67-yard drive that he capped with a tush push touchdown as time expired in the opening half. That proved to be the final points the Eagles scored on the night.

Sirianni had a different perspective on the pivotal hit on Hurts postgame compared with his initial reaction.

"Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline, ended up being a penalty," Sirianni said. "Obviously, you never want to see your quarterback get hit like that, but it's in the heat of the moment. I know nobody is trying to hurt anybody out there, and I always have remorse when I act that way. But I always love fighting for our players.

"I have to be more steady in that situation. ... I didn't like how I handled that."

articles.headline: Case Keenum drives Chicago to 3 touchdowns as the Bears beat the Eagles 27-7
articles.description: — Case Keenum was on target and on time all night long.
articles.headlineJa: ケース・キーナムが3TDを演出し、ベアーズが27-7でイーグルスを下す
articles.descriptionJa: 約3年ぶりの先発となったケース・キーナムが2つのタッチダウンパスを決め、シカゴ・ベアーズがジェイレン・ハーツ率いるフィラデルフィア・イーグルスを抑え込んでマンデーナイトで27-7の勝利を収めた。
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — Case Keenum was on target and on time all night long.


              It turns out the third-string quarterback for the Chicago Bears is pretty good, too.


              Keenum passed for two touchdowns in his first start in almost three years, and the Bears shut down Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles for a 27-7 victory on Monday night.


              Stepping in for Caleb Williams, Keenum was 24 for 34 for 247 yards. He also scored his first rushing touchdown since 2019 on a 1-yard plunge with 7:19 left, capping a 13-play drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock.


              “He knows where everyone is supposed to be on every single play and so he is really quick to recognize coverage,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “He knows why we’re calling the play and what we’re looking for and if we’re not getting that he’s accelerating through it really quickly. That’s what you get when you’re 15-plus years playing that position in this league.”


              It was Keenum’s first action since he started for Houston in a 36-22 loss to Cleveland on Dec. 24, 2023. Williams was sidelined by a right hamstring injury, and Tyson Bagent backed up Keenum after he cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


              “To get a shot again like this? Yeah, you dream of it,” Keenum said. “That’s why I'm still here doing this when I get knocked down. I got knocked down my whole career. I just keep getting up, coming to work, just keep bouncing back.”


              Kalif Raymond had six receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown as Chicago (2-1) rebounded from an ugly 9-3 loss to Minnesota.


              Philadelphia (2-1) turned the ball over three times and failed to record a takeaway for the third consecutive game to begin the season. Hurts was 16 for 25 for 153 yards, and Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 yards on 15 carries.


              “I think we all have to own that loss right there,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. “I don’t think anybody coached well. I don’t think anyone played well. It was a true team loss. And when it’s a true team loss, you know I have to look at myself first.”


              Down 20-7, the Eagles lined up to go for it on fourth-and-1 at their own 49 with about four minutes left in the third quarter. But Hurts was unable to draw a flag for offside, and the Eagles took a delay-of-game penalty before punting it away.


              Hurts was picked off by T.J. Edwards on a fourth-and-5 play from the Chicago 46 in the final minute of the third. Edwards dropped a potential interception on third down on Philadelphia’s first drive of the second half.


              “I liked the decision to go for it on fourth-and-5,” Sirianni said. “Hindsight, I feel like I should have went for it on that fourth-and-1 1/2.”

articles.headline: 'I love this game': Ben Simmons rejects NBA criticism
articles.description: A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.
articles.body:
A revitalised Ben Simmons has called "bull----" on critics who claim the reason he sat out the last NBA season is because he doesn't love basketball.

The Australian guard is back in the big league this year, having signed a $US3.5 million ($A4.9 million) deal with the Sacramento Kings.

Simmons purchased a controlling stake in a professional sport fishing team and didn't touch a basketball during his year off, in moves that drew plenty of criticism.

But the 30-year-old, who has been ravaged by injuries during his decade-long career, insists the break was purely about rebuilding his physical and mental health.

"It wasn't about if I wanted to play," Simmons told reporters at the Kings' preseason media session on Tuesday (AEST).

"All these people talk about how I don't love the game - that's bull----.

"I love this game. If I didn't, I wouldn't have taken that year to focus on myself and get back to where I'm at."

Simmons added he's not worried by critics chasing clicks from his name, declaring he's ready to prove to the world how much he missed basketball.

"I get to come out here and be creative and play hard and compete against a numerous amount of talented guys, so for me it's just in my blood and I've been doing it since I was a baby."

Simmons - a former No.1 overall draft pick, rookie of the year and three-time All-Star - believes the player he was at his peak "woke up" while he was out of the game.

And he's not short on confidence, bluntly outlining his personal goal this season.

"To dominate. Every time I step on the floor - to dominate," he said.

Simmons last played with the Los Angeles Clippers in April 2025 and took his year off as a result of persistent back and leg injuries, which took a significant toll on his body and mind.

The Melbourne-born star got serious in his comeback bid in August when he flew himself to a player-driven Boomers camp in his home town, where he impressed NBA scouts.

Sacramento pounced, signing Simmons on a one-season veteran league minimum deal.

"I'm right where I need to be," Simmons said.

"I took a lot of time to focus on my body over the season, and I think it's the best decision I've made for my career.

"I'm looking forward to getting going. I feel great, and I'm ready to go. No limitations."

Simmons expects to benefit from the low expectations on himself and the Kings, who were 22-60 last season and have only reached the playoffs once since 2006.

"It's really positive. There's no pressure," he said.

"They don't expect anything from us, so I think for us to go out there and show that we're capable of winning games and having a good team - that's doable.

"Based on this roster, I think we can do that."

Sacramento open the NBA preseason at home against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 5, and visit the Clippers for their regular-season opener on October 21.

articles.headline: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald says team still believes in RB Jadarian Price
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: シーホークスのマイク・マクドナルド監督、チームは今もRBジャダリアン・プライスを信頼していると語る
articles.descriptionJa: シーホークスのマイク・マクドナルド監督は、ドラフト1巡目指名のルーキーである先発ランニングバックのジャダリアン・プライスが日曜日に2週連続でファンブルロストを喫したものの、チームが彼への信頼を失っていないと述べた。
articles.body:
SEATTLE -- Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row Sunday.

"With JD, he understands what's going on," Macdonald said Monday. "He needs to take care of the ball. I think there's some things fundamentally where we can focus on. We're going to continue to give him the ball. We trust him, and we know he's going to work really hard to do his part as well."

Price's lost fumble in the first quarter Sunday gave the Washington Commanders a short field, setting up their first touchdown. It was one of three turnovers the Seahawks committed in a 33-31 loss that snapped their franchise-record 12-game winning streak.

When Price lost a fumble a week earlier in a win over the Arizona Cardinals, the Seahawks went right back to him on the first play of their next drive. But they didn't show the same patience Sunday. After Price's fumble at the 11:06 mark of the first quarter, his next carry wasn't until the 12:49 mark of the third quarter, though he was targeted twice in that span.

Price finished with five carries for 15 yards, plus one catch for 7 yards. Despite making his third straight start, he played 19 of Seattle's 67 offensive snaps, while Emanuel Wilson (nine carries for 14 yards) and George Holani (eight touches for 58 yards) each played 24 snaps.

"I think just, as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Macdonald said postgame. "I know he didn't come back after the initial fumble. We decided to calm it down and bring him back after the half, but he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out. He'll be fine."

Price fumbled five times over three seasons as a backup at Notre Dame.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, have not dealt with this problem in recent years. Kenneth Walker III, whom Price was drafted to replace, fumbled only three times over four seasons with Seattle but did not lose any of them. Zach Charbonnet, who co-started in 2025 alongside Walker, did not fumble over his first three seasons.

Price, who was selected with the 32nd pick, has 119 yards on 28 attempts (4.3 average) over three games, plus four catches for 21 yards. He has yet to score an NFL touchdown.

"JD is such a great, great dude," quarterback Sam Darnold said postgame. "And he knows his responsibility. He knows not to turn the ball over, so there's not much you say to him. You just tell him, 'Keep going, and we've got your back.'"

Macdonald said the Seahawks will decide by Tuesday whether to open Charbonnet's 21-day practice window this week. Charbonnet is on the physically unable to perform list after having ACL surgery in February. He has to spend at least one more game on the PUP list, but he has been eligible to begin practicing as of last week.

articles.headline: Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'
articles.description: Bronny James said he hasn't spoken much to his father, LeBron, about the decision to leave the Lakers this summer, but said he's excited to face him on Christmas.
articles.headlineJa: ブロニー、レブロン・ジェームズのレイカーズ退団に「父には父の道がある」
articles.descriptionJa: ブロニー・ジェームズは、この夏にレイカーズを離れるという父レブロンの決断について本人とあまり話していないとしつつも、クリスマスに対戦するのが楽しみだと語った。
articles.body:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- When LeBron James left the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son and teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So, it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path, and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself, and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So, he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history. Whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father-and-son duo entered the game together or last season in the playoffs, when they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency where the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Bronny James, whose $2.3 million contract for this season is guaranteed, said that he has spent the summer focusing on his role backing up Lakers guards Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Bronny played in 42 games last season and eight playoff games.

"You guys know me as Bronny. My real name is LeBron. I've been doing this for however long," Bronny James said. "It's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron."

Though LeBron and Bronny might not have spoken about the move much, Bronny wishes his father well and is looking forward to the first time the Lakers face the 76ers this season, on Christmas in L.A.

"I'm happy for him and excited to see where their season goes," Bronny James said. "I'm excited to see him on Christmas. I'm excited to play against him on Christmas, so that's going to be good."

Not having LeBron is a significant adjustment for the Lakers and his son. L.A. has nine new players and is trying to focus on this season and not on the past. It is the start of the first season without LeBron since 2017-18.

"It was kind of sad [that he left]; playing with LeBron was amazing," Doncic said about James' departure. "There's a lot of things I learned from him, and we all know who LeBron James is. We spent time together, and it was amazing."
